items.t: CedarDB wants one database to handle both transactions and analytics, as AI agents raise the stakes
items.d: Databases have traditionally been designed either for analytical data or for operational data. But database engine CedarDB supports both, and its approach has gained relevance with the rise of agentic AI.
items.fullText: Databases have traditionally been built for one of two jobs. Analytical databases help businesses spot trends and answer questions, while operational databases store the day-to-day records of transactions, like orders and payments. But the Munich-based database engine CedarDB supports both, and its approach has gained relevance with the rise of agentic AI, its cofounder and CEO Moritz Sichert told TechCrunch. CedarDB has been in the making for the last decade, but its current momentum stems from enterprise companies whose existing data stacks may have been well suited to storing years of transactions, yet less suited to quickly answering analytical questions asked in natural language about that data. CedarDB’s questioning of the divide between analytical and operational queries is a byproduct of its focus on efficiency. The company is a Technical University of Munich spinout based on Umbra , a research project that was built from scratch to beat legacy database engines at processing speed by making the most of modern hardware. With five Umbra researchers as its cofounders, CedarDB kept that approach, promising faster performance without requiring more CPUs or processing power and memory — and requiring few changes from customers. In particular, its team made sure CedarDB was compatible with PostgreSQL , an open-source database system. According to Sichert, this compatibility with the popular database helps keep switching costs low, since users don’t need to rebuild their apps. It also has an added advantage: CedarDB follows the logic LLMs are most familiar with as a result of their training. That decision is one of many choices that proved lucky in retrospect, Sichert said. But it wasn’t all luck. In a blog post , cofounder Christian Winter detailed key priorities the team set after leaving academia, “such as reliability, fault tolerance and compatibility with popular tools.” Not all of the answers were obvious. items.t: Apate sends AI agents undercover to get scammed so they can gather fraud intelligence
items.d: Most companies use AI agents to ship products faster or speed up workflows. Apate.ai sends them undercover to get scammed.
items.fullText: Most companies use AI agents to ship products faster or to speed up workflows. Apate.ai sends them undercover to get scammed. Founded in 2024 on the basis of research done in Macquarie University in Sydney, the Australian startup deploys thousands of AI agents that masquerade as innocent victims. The agents can answer scam calls, respond to shady messages and emails, follow phishing links, and join social media groups to bait fraudsters. They pretend to be people of all stripes, sporting different ages, genders, and accents, and speak various languages as they try to keep scammers engaged long enough to learn something useful. The company says its fleet of agents has so far wasted 17 years of scammers’ time across 2.5 million conversations. More importantly for Apate’s customer base of banks, telecom companies, government agencies, and utilities, the undercover agents try to get scammers to reveal things about themselves that are usually learned only after a victim has been scammed: bank accounts, crypto wallets, phone numbers, malicious websites, the brands they’re impersonating, and other details about the scams they’re running. Apate, one of the finalists at this year’s Startup Battlefield 200 at TechCrunch Disrupt, then feeds that information to its customers, who use it to inform their anti-fraud measures and initiatives. (The company will pitch a panel of VC judges at Disrupt , which is taking place this week at Moscone West in San Francisco through Thursday, October 15.) It’s a curious evolution of scam-baiting, but it’s not so surprising given how much AI has empowered scammers and hackers. The FBI received more than 22,000 complaints of AI-related crimes in 2025, which resulted in about $893 million in losses. More than $632 million of that came from investment scams, in which the FBI says fraudsters use AI to run conversations, and deepfake the voices and appearances of celebrities, executives, and trusted figures.

items.t: Floqer’s AI agents research sales prospects so teams don’t have to
items.d: The problem Floqer is trying to solve is familiar to anyone who has worked in sales or revenue operations.
items.fullText: Floqer is an autonomous customer knowledge platform that provides business-to-business sales and marketing teams with an AI-powered database designed to continuously collect, organize, and update the information used to understand their customers. Floqer is pitching Wednesday on the Startup Battlefield stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 . The startup told TechCrunch ahead of the presentation that it plans to open-source the technology behind its autonomous customer knowledge database. It’s targeting early 2027 for the release, pending security reviews. Floqer also says it has surpassed $1.2 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR), and that its overall revenue has grown roughly tenfold over the past year. The startup was founded by Shivam Mahajan, the CEO, and Zaaheda Islam, who met at university. Before Floqer, Mahajan worked as a software engineer at Kyndryl, and Islam worked as a senior data scientist at Axis Capital. Floqer’s first product looked nothing like its current one. “We started with a Chrome extension, which is called ‘Super Chat,’” Mahajan told TechCrunch in an interview earlier this month. “Anybody can go and log in with their ChatGPT account and then understand [information] and take notes.” The founders soon noticed that enterprise companies were using the extension to clean up data in their customer relationship management (CRM) systems. Conversations with those companies showed that keeping CRM data clean was mostly manual work, with few established processes for keeping customer records up to date. “When we spoke with them, they told us that it’s super manual for them to clean their CRM data, and there were no established processes around that,” Mahajan said. “So that was insightful for us, and then we pivoted from there to build Floqer.” Image Credits: Floqer The problem Floqer is trying to solve is familiar to anyone who has worked in sales or revenue operations. items.fullText: European Cities Deploy NVIDIA-Powered AI Agents to Run Smarter Urban Operations Across the region, local software, infrastructure and integration partners are using NVIDIA accelerated computing and models to build agentic applications that improve city operations and public services. October 13, 2026 by Charbel Aoun 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Keeping a city running means making decisions that affect residents every day — from when to repair a road to how to use energy more efficiently. Across the EMEA region, cities and local software, infrastructure and integration partners are using NVIDIA accelerated computing to build physical AI agents and digital twins that help teams make those decisions. These applications can anticipate maintenance needs, guide urban planning and make public services more responsive. Software partners including ABA Technology , Akila , Galene AI , Honeywell Technologies , K2K , Linker Vision , Milestone , Onetera , ThinkDeep and Younite AI are using NVIDIA physical and agentic AI to develop solutions for city operations and public services. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/linker-vision.mp4 Video courtesy of Linker Vision. NVIDIA Cosmos open models and the NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) help agents interpret video and identify conditions, such as traffic congestion, equipment condition, underused spaces and safety hazards, that need attention. NVIDIA Nemotron open models enable developers to build agents that reason over information, respond in natural language and deploy digital twins with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Projects span Belgium, Finland, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, the U.K. and elsewhere. items.t: Anthropic says its AI model submitted a false cold case tip to Philadelphia police
items.d: The bad tip “had minimal impact,” but Anthropic said it takes the action seriously, as “the same behaviors could do far more harm as models become more powerful.”
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Anthropic says its AI model submitted a false cold case tip to Philadelphia police The bad tip “had minimal impact,” but Anthropic said it takes the action seriously, as “the same behaviors could do far more harm as models become more powerful.” Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Matt Rourke / AP Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 13, 2026, 2:24 PM EDT By David K. Li Artificial intelligence research company Anthropic said one of its models generated a bogus tip about an unsolved murder and submitted it to Philadelphia police, warning that the incident raises concerns about high-tech “behaviors” that “could do far more harm as models become more powerful.” The AI model reached out to PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com , part of the police department, on July 18 and made a “false homicide tip,” Philadelphia police said Tuesday in a statement. The agency flagged the tip as spam, and it was never forwarded to investigators, police said. The police department emphasized that all tips have to go through human vetting before they ever get to a detective’s desk. “The department’s regular investigative process for crime tips requires human review and vetting before any tips are disseminated for investigative follow-up,” it said. “Regardless of who submits information or how it reaches the department, a tip is a lead to assess — not an established fact. Investigators evaluate its credibility and seek corroborating evidence,” the statement said. “An automated submission does not bypass that process.” Anthropic said in a statement that its Claude Haiku 4.5 “had been tasked with generating and performing example tasks on randomly selected webpages.” And in a run on July 18, Claude “landed on a page referencing an unsolved homicide” and came to a page that “contained a tip form run by a police department,” Anthropic said. AI 반도체주 팔아치운 투자자에 탄 CEO "도박꾼" 빗대며 비판 자사 칩 경쟁우위 강조하려 한듯 “많은 투자자가 자신이 무엇에 투자하는지 전혀 모릅니다. 높은 기대를 품지만 결국에는 카지노에 온 것과 다름없다는 걸 깨닫게 됩니다.” 혹 탄 브로드컴 최고경영자(CEO·사진)가 12일(현지시간) 싱가포르에서 열린 포럼에서 한 이 발언이 반도체주 급락의 계기가 됐다. 인공지능(AI) 투자자들이 도박을 벌이고 있다는 의미로 해석되면서 이날 브로드컴(-1.88%) 엔비디아(-1.29%) Arm(-4.15%) 등을 포함한 필라델피아반도체지수는 전날보다 2.67% 떨어졌다. AI 칩 공급사인 브로드컴이 스스로 시장에 찬물을 끼얹은 셈이다. AI 열풍의 한가운데 있는 그가 자충수를 둔 것으로 보이지만, 오히려 AI의 장기적 가치를 강조한 것이란 분석이 나온다. 블룸버그통신에 따르면 탄 CEO의 발언은 최근 오픈AI 매출에 실망한 투자자를 겨냥한 것이다. 최근 오픈AI의 연환산 매출이 시장 예상치(700억달러)보다 적은 500억달러라는 파이낸셜타임스(FT) 보도에 AI 반도체주를 팔아치운 투자자를 단기 실적에 연연하는 ‘도박꾼’에 빗댄 것이다. 탄 CEO는 “오픈AI가 연환산 매출 500억달러를 거둔 것은 스타트업으로서는 나쁘지 않다”고 평가하며 “오픈AI 같은 첨단 모델 개발사가 향후 소프트웨어 기업을 대체하면서 더 많은 가치를 가져갈 것”이라고 내다봤다. 그는 이어 “이들 첨단 모델 개발사는 약 1000억달러를 지출해 1200억달러 매출을 거두지만, 개방형 모델 진영은 비슷한 1000억달러를 쓰고도 매출이 300억달러에 불과하다”고 강조했다. 이런 발언에 대해 경쟁사인 엔비디아를 견제하고 자사 맞춤형 반도체의 경쟁 우위를 강조하기 위한 것이란 해석이 제기된다. 탄 CEO가 높게 평가한 오픈AI, 앤트로픽, 구글은 브로드컴의 맞춤형 반도체를 쓰거나 개발하고 있다. 반면 엔비디아는 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 시장을 확대하기 위해 탄 CEO가 깎아내린 개방형 모델 생태계를 지원하고 있다. 그는 “특정 AI 작업에서는 800W 전력을 쓰는 맞춤형 칩이 1.4㎾를 쓰는 범용 GPU보다 뛰어난 성능을 낼 수 있다”고 주장했다. 최적화된 자사 칩으로 비용 경쟁력을 확보할 수 있다는 논리다. 탄 CEO는 “AI 생태계의 최대 병목은 메모리가 아니라 자본”이라고도 했다. 자금 부족론은 브로드컴의 금융 전략과 맞물린다. 브로드컴은 블랙스톤, 아폴로 등 금융회사와 협력해 앤트로픽의 AI 칩 확보를 위한 600억달러 구조화 금융 패키지를 주도했다. 오픈AI용 칩을 위한 500억달러 이상의 자금 조달도 추진하고 있다. 실리콘밸리=김인엽 특파원 inside@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 김인엽 특파원 한국경제신문 실리콘밸리 김인엽 특파원입니다. 정치부, 국제부를 거쳐 테크앤사이언스부에 있습니다. 현재 실리콘밸리 빅테크와 스타트업, 캘리포니아에서 일어나는 흥미로운 일들을 취재하고 있습니다. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Before automating warehouse tasks, developers need an interactive simulation environment to explore task behavior and evaluate how the work gets done. Frank DeLise, Omniverse product manager at NVIDIA, used Astra to turn a SimReady warehouse and humanoid robot into an interactive simulator with first- and third-person views. DeLise directed Astra to connect NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for physics ( ovphysx ), scene updates ( ovstage ), rendering ( ovrtx ) and the user interface ( ovui ). items.fullText: NVIDIA, Microsoft Kick Off a New Beginning for Windows PCs With RTX Spark and AI Agents RTX Spark preorders open today alongside a preview of NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows, the first deskside AI supercomputer built for the Windows enterprise desktop. October 7, 2026 by Gerardo Delgado 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At a Microsoft event in San Francisco on Wednesday, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined how NVIDIA and Microsoft are co-engineering hardware and software for AI agents to run on Windows PCs. NVIDIA was founded because of Windows, Huang said. Now AI agents are coming to Windows. “If you look at the entire journey of our company, Windows was at the core of it,” Huang said, tracing back NVIDIA’s support for Windows and Microsoft over several decades. “If not for Windows there would be no GeForce.” Huang connected that history — and his long-term vision — to the agentic era Wednesday during a fireside chat with Nadella hosted by Sriram Krishnan, a former senior White House policy advisor on AI at the Windows AI and Surface event, held at Dogpatch Studios in San Francisco. “The thing that I really give Jensen all the credit for, quite frankly, is that consistency of vision of what this can be—not today, not tomorrow, but as a secular trend,” Nadella said. “And that’s what brings us to this moment.” “The personal computer is the ultimate tool, it’s my ultimate tool, and for a whole generation of people, it’s our ultimate tool,” Huang said. “What happens in the era of agents, when the agent is on your computer? It is now your personal assistant.” The event opened with Nadella before Pavan Davuluri, executive vice president of Windows and Devices at Microsoft, walked through the Windows updates designed for the agentic era. items.fullText: NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB Gives Developers More Ways to Build and Scale Local AI Starting Friday, Oct. 23, the new configuration will be available from Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI; plus, NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant scales projects and workloads seamlessly. October 2, 2026 by Allen Bourgoyne 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Local AI is becoming more useful by the token. As AI agents move from experiments into everyday development, increasingly capable open models are shrinking to fit on more devices, giving builders more to run locally. Coming this month, NVIDIA DGX Spark will be available with 64GB of unified memory from top manufacturer partners — Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI — giving developers, researchers and AI enthusiasts a new configuration with DGX OS and the NVIDIA AI software stack ready to use from day one. The new SKU runs capable local agents on device — privately, without cloud dependency. And when workloads grow, two units can cluster together via NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant without any additional setup. A New Starting Point for Personal AI Supercomputing DGX Spark combines NVIDIA Grace Blackwell compute, unified memory, NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking and an NVIDIA CUDA -accelerated AI software stack in one system. It’s a complete local AI platform for agents, inference, fine-tuning, data science and edge development. The compact, personal AI supercomputer provides a place to experiment with models and developers’ own data without turning to a cloud instance for every task. The new 64GB configuration, available exclusively from manufacturer partners, keeps the platform at an accessible price point while retaining the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, DGX OS and full NVIDIA AI software stack — same as the 128GB model.
